text:
alex.cruz: Quick question following the hotplug RFC — how do we want to handle namespace collisions when two allocations try to hot-swap the same logical weight name concurrently?
priya: Good callout. Current naive plan is last-writer-wins at the namespace layer, but that feels risky for live traffic.
jason: Agreed, LWW could silently break canaries. We discussed leases in the RFC, right? Short lease + owner tombstone might help.
marta: Leases + compare-and-swap on the manifest entry would give us atomic handoff. But we need a fallback if the client only has manifestless shards (safetensors stream).
kai: For manifestless we could version the shard blob with an append-only header: `v=42;nonce=...;sig=...` and require the loader to validate version bump. If two sides race, the loader rejects the older nonce.
priya: That demands signing for all vendors. Is that acceptable? Enterprise/private users might be fine but hosted API needs to interop with public stores.
jason: We can make signing optional. Fallback path: the warmup coordinator takes a lease and does the atomic swap in the batch layer, not the object store. So clients without signed manifests still go through coordinator-protected handoff.
alex.cruz: Sketch of decision: 1) Lease at namespace index + CAS manifest update for manifested checkpoints. 2) For manifestless, require coordinator lease for hot-swap. 3) Signed headers optional but recommended for cross-region fast failover. Sound right?
marta: Sounds good. One nuance: coordinator lease durability — it must survive controller restarts. Use DB-backed lease (etcd/pg) with TTL and renewal.
kai: Also need to tie eviction policy to lease priority. Hotplug of a large shard should bump a reservation so eviction doesn't reclaim it mid-copy. Could be `reservation = max(reservation, lease_priority)` on the cache slab.
priya: Nice. And add a small backpressure window: if the loader sees >N concurrent hot-swap attempts for same model, return 429 with hint header `X-Hotplug-Retry-After: 150` and let coordinator serialize.
jason: Implementation note: make the coordinator endpoint idempotent: `POST /hotplug/swap` with body `{ model, namespace, expected_version?, lease_ttl }` returns `{ status, lease_id, applied_version }` and is safe to retry.
alex.cruz: Can someone open a tiny follow-up RFC for: lease schema, coordinator REST API, and cache-reservation semantics? Keep it short — just enough for eng-sre to implement.
marta: I can draft it. Will add an example flow for safetensors streaming case.
priya: Also add tests: race between two hotplugs, coordinator crash during swap, and eviction bump regression.
warmup-bot: :white_check_mark: warmup job enqueued for model=galaxy-3b shard=layer.42 lease=auto ttl=60s (job id: wj-20240315-881)
kai: One more thought — telemetry. Emit events: `hotplug.request`, `hotplug.lease.grant`, `hotplug.swap.applied`, `hotplug.swap.rejected` with dimensions (model, namespace, region, lease_owner). We'll need these for SLO debugging.
jason: +1, and include `applied_version` in the swap.applied event so we can correlate with traces.
alex.cruz: Thanks all. Marta — assign me as reviewer. Priya/Jason — add the test cases to the ticket. I'll put the RFC link here when draft exists: https://rfc.internal/++/hotplug-lease-2024
priya: ack. Short follow-up: do we want to block warmup if namespace is under a canary flag? i.e., don't let hotplug change active slot during canary window.
marta: Yes, coordinator should accept an optional `canary_window` param and then set `canary_hold=true` in the lease so the router can keep traffic pinned.
kai: Router change is tiny: honor `canary_hold` and treat the new version as non-live until router flips.
jason: I'll file the router PR after the RFC.
alex.cruz: Cool. I'll wait for the draft. If no major objections, we'll land leases + coordinator pattern as the short-term plan. :thumbsup:
